issue_context.title: Extend the capability of `scheduler_perf` to support customized configuration
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

#### What would you like to be added:
Extend the capability of `scheduler_perf` to support customized configuration.
#### Why is this needed:
Currently, `scheduler_perf` start scheduler with the default configuration, 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c78f67a005977bf1159b538a33c2ee3bf5ca24da/test/integration/util/util.go#L86-L90

The above snippet of code creates a scheduler with all the default options, 
```options := defaultSchedulerOptions```

This make it impossible to benchmark the performance of certain plugins where a  non-default `PluginConfig` is required, e.g. `serviceaffinity` require the `args.AffinityLabels`  to be set.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c78f67a005977bf1159b538a33c2ee3bf5ca24da/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/serviceaffinity/service_affinity.go#L236-L238


Thus, in order to support the above case,  it might be good to enhance `scheduler_perf` to consume a separate scheduler config file, just like what scheduler does today.

We can provide more benchmark schema / testcases after this feature is provided.

@ahg-g @alculquicondor @Huang-Wei Do you have any comments on this? thanks!

/sig scheduling
comments:
The request seems reasonable. But I don't have experience adding command line flags to tests. Just make sure it works with the default configuration if nothing is passed.

/triage accepted
It doesn't need to be a command line flag, it could be a config file that the test always loads if it exists, just like the tests configuration yamls.

I don't have a strong option on an internal scheduler CC config variable vs. CLI argument. But it'd be favorable to make it aligned with configFile (`config/performance-config.yaml`) - i.e., either make both configFile and the new scheduler CC config internal variables, or both as CLI arguments.

BTW: currently the only CLI arg we have is `dataItemsDir`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/983272ce6a0c5df631871c01a8148438ff963245/test/integration/scheduler_perf/util.go#L53

Thanks guys for the input, I am thinking it's not necessary a CLI arg, but just a new field in the `testCase` struct, might be `schedulerConf`?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/27c89b9aec73f66529a497910c460af2b25ab6dd/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L63-L80

If this field is set, then load the config file and pass down to scheduler instantiation, I will work out a POC first.


/assign

> It doesn't need to be a command line flag, it could be a config file that the test always loads if it exists, just like the tests configuration yamls.

+1

+1 to the enhancement

>a new field in the testCase struct, might be schedulerConf

This has a limitation: you'd need to modify each test if you want to run all tests with a different scheduler config. I instead propose an environment variable that is understood by scheduler_perf (same idea as the command line flag basically). Something like this maybe?

```
$ SCHEDULER_PERF_CONFIG=config/custom-config.yaml go test -timeout=600s <... rest of the args...>
```

if the `SCHEDULER_PERF_CONFIG` envvar is unspecified, the test loads the default configuration
isn't a command line argument more standard?
It is, but arg parsing is tricky with `go test` IME. However if @chendave prefers and wants to implement an argument, I'll have no problems :)

> This has a limitation: you'd need to modify each test if you want to run all tests with a different scheduler config.

Actually, there is no need to modify each test, but only the testcase that need a different scheduler config.

review_comments: nit: move this section below L385.
Done
I think if you pass this, you don't need to set the gvk, but you can check.
verified, this doesn't work without gvk being set, I will dive into the `decode` method to have a double check in my next day.
ah, makes sense, we need a version to apply the defaults

The logic here first instantiates an up-to-date versioned CC, and calls scheme.Default() to apply default values, and finally convert it back to an unversioned CC. @adtac @alculquicondor could you confirm it's the best practice so far to instantiate a default unversioned CC?

This is what scheduler does today,  pls let me know whether you want this method public and import it from there.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fcee7a01050652e54d2819b1942533d96e40f455/cmd/kube-scheduler/app/options/options.go#L137-L147
Yes, this is how I'd do it too. We only have defaulting for the versioned types, so there's no way to directly apply defaults to the internal type.
`scheduler.New` already knows how to handle defaults... why do it again?

there's more to using the v1beta1 defaults than what `defaultSchedulerOptions` offers. for example we have default QPS limits set in the v1beta1 defaults.go (which we don't use here right now, but will in the future (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99638#discussion_r593025201)), but scheduler_perf should respect that in the future. the `scheduler.New` defaults won't give you that IIUC.
Then just use Decode https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fcee7a01050652e54d2819b1942533d96e40f455/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L411-L412

> there's more to using the v1beta1 defaults than what defaultSchedulerOptions offers

+1, hope this answer your question?  @alculquicondor

The second reason why I add this in the first place is because when the `config` is `nil`,  `schedulerOptions` will be overridden even though `scheduler.New` has defined the default options, for example, if create an empty `KubeSchedulerConfiguration` obj instead of setting it as default, `cfg.Profiles` will override the default value .
We should make sure those options as least have a default value set in this case.

```
	options := defaultSchedulerOptions
	for _, opt := range opts {
		opt(&options)
	}
```

How the config handled here is a little different with scheduler to simplify the implementation.

> Then just use Decode

well, both of the methods can be used to set the default options, but the `Decode` here will decode into `runtime.Object`

```
func (c *codec) Decode(data []byte, defaultGVK *schema.GroupVersionKind, into runtime.Object) (runtime.Object, *schema.GroupVersionKind, error)
```

There is no conversion provided to convert `runtime.Object` into internal `KubeSchedulerConfiguration`, but we still need to create a un-versioned scheduler config.

Besides, I not sure why you suggest to use `Decode`, am I miss something?

`runtime.Object` is just an interface for any API type, including `KubeSchedulerConfiguration`. Again, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fcee7a01050652e54d2819b1942533d96e40f455/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L411-L412 as an example.

One question: should we honor QPS and other settings in given `config`? If so, `config` is unversioned, which implied each field employs a concrete value, then if `config` is not nil, how can we decide to derive the values in `config` vs. apply the values specified here (5000)?
we can take this as a default value, and override this value if CC has a value defined, maybe we can drop a TODO item here and address it in the v1.22?
mark this resolved, feel free to drop any comments anyway.
It seems we do not fully respect `config` - we're just using partial fields related to scheduler. Let's add a comment here.
true, will do.
